messages.content: We talked it over. For St. Pete, Gulf-side beats the bigger inland suite. Can you help me move this from comparison to booking before that cancellable family room disappears?

Yes. I would book the Tampa version, not Sarasota: ATL to TPA Thursday morning, TPA to ATL late Sunday afternoon, assigned-seat economy rather than basic economy, and the cancellable Gulf-side family room. The two choices still open are the car and the balcony upcharge. Before you pay the hotel, verify resort fee, taxes, paid breakfast pricing, parking fee, bed setup, mini-fridge, cancellation deadline, and whether the balcony category is actually guaranteed.
If Delta is still close, use Delta. I do not want to save a few dollars and then have seat assignment problems with the three of us.

Delta Main Cabin is the cleaner pick here. It is about $34 total more than the cheapest basic-style option, but it includes standard seat selection. Current workable flights: Thu Aug 6 ATL 9:20 a.m. to TPA 10:52 a.m.; Sun Aug 9 TPA 4:55 p.m. to ATL 6:28 p.m. Both are nonstop and the Sunday return still avoids a late bedtime.
Good. What about the rental car? We had said no full-trip car, but with groceries and possible storms I am second-guessing it.

This would be a change from the earlier no-car version, but it makes sense if you want flexibility. Side by side: no car means lower cost and no parking fee, but you are relying on rideshares, booster logistics, and weather timing. A cancellable midsize car is about $180 for the trip, plus roughly $84 hotel parking and a small toll estimate; it makes the grocery stop, rainy-day backup, and airport timing easier. I would add the midsize only if it is pay-later and cancellable.
Add it, pay-later only. We can bring our travel booster. Is the balcony worth paying for?

Not unless the hotel confirms the exact room category. The family room near the beach is the scarce piece. The balcony upcharge appears to be for a partial Gulf-view category, but the booking language does not clearly say every room in that category has a private balcony. I would book the cancellable family room now, skip or hold off on the balcony upcharge, and call the hotel directly about balcony guarantee, bed configuration, and fridge.
Seats next. I want our child between us or right next to both of us. If I can get the window, great, but together matters more.

Use three-across rows. Outbound, take 18A, 18B, 18C: you at the window, child in the middle, spouse on the aisle. Return, take 20A, 20B, 20C. If either row disappears while you are checking out, choose any three adjacent seats before chasing a window seat.
Okay. I booked the Delta flights, the cancellable Gulf-side room, and the pay-later midsize car. Before I close everything, what should I save or still check?

Save screenshots or PDFs for the airline confirmation, seat assignments, hotel cancellation terms, rental car pickup details, and the hotel address. Still call the hotel to verify: total resort fee and taxes, nightly parking charge, breakfast cost, whether the family room has a mini-fridge, exact beds or sleeper setup, pool and beach access rules, luggage storage, and whether any balcony room is truly guaranteed before paying more. For the car, note that you are bringing your own booster and check whether tolls are billed by plate or require an add-on.

messages.content: We are two days out for St. Pete. Can you give me the practical checklist? The return time shifted a little and the forecast is all thunderstorms.

The return shift is manageable: it now leaves TPA about 5:18 p.m. and lands around 6:51 p.m., so it still works for bedtime. Seats 18A-C outbound and 20A-C return are still the best free adjacent sets; I would not split up for the slightly closer window pair that opened.
Good. We have one checked bag and the booster. What time should we leave Decatur?

For the 9:20 a.m. ATL flight, aim to be at the airport by 7:25. Leave Decatur around 6:35, earlier if traffic looks messy. Check in tonight, add the checked bag if the app price is the same or better, and keep the booster with the car-seat gear rather than packing it deep.
What is the TPA arrival plan if the room is not ready?

Pick up the midsize car, take the toll route if traffic favors it, and keep pool clothes in a day tote. Stop for groceries before the hotel, then use luggage storage if the room is not ready. Early check-in is not guaranteed, but the hotel confirmed luggage storage, pool access, paid parking, and the pool itself. Lightning can pause pool time, so do not promise immediate swimming.
Breakfast is still paid at the hotel, right? I would rather not do that every morning.

Right, treat hotel breakfast as the weather backup. Grocery stop: yogurt, fruit, cereal bars, water, and coffee supplies if the room has a maker. Use a nearby cafe for one morning if the forecast gives you a clear window.
First night dinner and rain backups?

Book an indoor, walkable dinner around 6:15 or 6:30 so you are not driving again after beach traffic. Rain backups: Dali Museum, the aquarium, Sunken Gardens if it is only cloudy, or a short arcade/ice cream stop near the beach. Recheck tonight and tomorrow morning: flight status, gate, seat map, rental pickup hours, toll policy, hotel parking fee, beach flags, and whether there is any weather waiver.

messages.content: Switching gears after Florida: I have a Minneapolis client training visit coming up Monday September 14 through Thursday September 17. Can you help me frame the travel plan before I send anything for approval?

Yes. The big unknowns are the exact site, whether Monday has an in-person start, Thursday end time, and whether you need a car. If the site is downtown, I would look near the training center and rely on rideshare or light rail. If it is the hospital or university area, I would look near campus and only add a rental car if the client expects movement between buildings or off-site meetings.
That is the problem. They may use a downtown training center or a room near the university hospital. Monday might be a welcome meeting, or it may stay remote until Tuesday.

Then I would not lock the final booking yet. Flight windows: if Monday in-person starts after 1 p.m., same-day ATL to MSP around 8:30 a.m. works without a painfully early start. If Monday starts before noon, fly Sunday evening and add one hotel night. If Monday is remote, a late-morning Monday flight is possible, but it creates awkward check-in and work-space issues.
For MSP I would prefer a nonstop if the timing is decent. Delta is fine if it is not absurd.

Nonstop is realistic from ATL. Provisional outbound options: Sunday evening around 6 p.m. if you need to be fresh Monday morning, Monday around 8:30 a.m. if first in-person is early afternoon, or Monday around 11 a.m. only if the day stays remote. I would avoid a 6 a.m. departure unless the client confirms a Monday morning on-site requirement.
Thursday return should not make me bolt out of the room. I hate leaving a client session half-packed.

For the return, I would hold two rules: if the client ends by 2:30 p.m., take a late-afternoon nonstop around 5 p.m.; if they end closer to 4 or 5, take an evening nonstop and accept the later arrival. I would not book a 3 p.m. return unless Thursday becomes a half-day.
Hotels: I need a well-reviewed place, easy mornings, and dinner nearby. Breakfast included would be a plus, not a dealbreaker.

Shortlist by site. Downtown option: a well-rated business hotel near the training center, stronger dinner access, breakfast likely paid. University/hospital option: a Hampton Inn or Hilton Garden Inn style property near campus, usually simpler breakfast and easier hospital access, but fewer dinner choices immediately outside. If the site is unknown, choose a cancellable hotel in the more likely area or wait 24 hours for the client to confirm.
Would you route both versions for approval or just ask the client first?

Ask the client first, then route one primary version plus a fallback note. The approval package should say the flight will be Monday morning if the first required on-site time is after 1 p.m.; otherwise Sunday evening. For hotel, it should say downtown if the training center is confirmed, university area if the hospital room is confirmed.
What exactly should I ask the client coordinator? I want one email, not a back-and-forth.

Ask for: exact street address for each training day, first required in-person time Monday, final end time Thursday, whether there is a Thursday debrief that can run late, badge or security arrival buffer, whether they recommend downtown versus university hotels, parking availability, whether rideshare is acceptable, whether a rental car is reimbursable, and whether any evening client dinner is planned.
Can you give me the provisional plan I can paste under that email after they answer?

Provisional plan: ATL-MSP nonstop, preferably Monday morning around 8:30 a.m. if the first on-site item starts after 1 p.m.; Sunday evening fallback if Monday begins before noon. Return MSP-ATL nonstop Thursday late afternoon if sessions end by 2:30 p.m.; evening fallback if the day runs later. Hotel will be cancellable and at least solidly reviewed, with breakfast or easy nearby breakfast noted and dinner access checked. Rental car stays undecided until the site, parking, and between-site movement are confirmed.
